Second, a glycosylation/lipidation site sits directly on the modeled interface, and AF3 does not represent glycans, so even the extracellular part of the contact is unreliable. The other evidence gives no support to offset this. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed all found nothing for the pair. HPA enrichment does not overlap (mesothelial cells for TNFRSF8; mast cells, bone marrow and lymphoid tissue for GPR65). GPR65 is mainly vesicular while TNFRSF8 is at the plasma membrane. With a topologically impossible model and no independent support, INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE understated the problem. The confidence is medium rather than high because the topology violation shows the model is wrong, not that the proteins can never interact through a correctly oriented ectodomain contact.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: Both proteins are glycoproteins (TNFRSF8 4 sites, GPR65 3 sites). The fold check shows a glycosylation/lipidation site directly on the modeled interface, and AF3 does not model glycans, so the contact is unreliable.
cooccurrence_evidence: 0 PubMed papers mention TNFRSF8 and GPR65 together.
known_interaction_evidence: STRING: no association. CellPhoneDB: none (GPR65 not in gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. known_interaction_strength=none.
follow_up: If this pair is still of interest, re-fold only the extracellular domains with glycans represented, and test co-expression in activated lymphocytes.

rationale: I'm changing the verdict from CONFIRMED_NOVEL to IMPLAUSIBLE. The check is right that HPA gives no protein-level tissue shared by ROR2 and MRGPRF, and neither is secreted, so a direct contact would need both in the same membrane of the same cell. My earlier argument rested on overlapping bone marrow MSC enrichment, which is RNA or single-cell level and weaker than shared protein-level data. Both being plasma-membrane receptors only makes a cis interaction possible in principle. Nothing independent supports it: STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed co-occurrence were all empty (known_interaction_strength=none), and no AF3 fold was run to give structural support (fold_evidence_status=not_run). The AF3 numbers I cited earlier (ipTM 0.66, interface pLDDT ~60, 6079 Å2 buried) were moderate and looked like non-specific packing without a bilayer. I keep confidence low because the MSC single-cell overlap leaves a small chance of real co-expression.

follow_up: Only worth revisiting if single-cell or protein-level data show ROR2 and MRGPRF in the same cell type. In that case, re-run AF3 with a membrane-aware setup and with the glycans represented.

rationale: Both are 7-TM GPCRs with non-overlapping expression: GRM8 is enriched in choroid plexus epithelial cells and cerebral cortex, MRGPRX2 only in mast cells (UniProt: mast cell-specific). A GPCR-GPCR interface this large (BSA 3883 Å2, 1007 contacts) at only moderate interface pLDDT (60.5) is most likely cis packing of the transmembrane bundles, which requires both receptors in the same cell membrane, and nothing here supports that. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed all return nothing for the pair, so it is novel but lacks biological support.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: GRM8 is a UniProt Glycoprotein with 5 N-glycosylation sites (presumably in its large extracellular domain) and 8 disulfide bonds. MRGPRX2 has no annotated glycosylation, only 2 disulfide bonds. The PubMed PTM hits for both genes are non-specific (MRGPRX2 mast-cell activation papers; unrelated GRM8 papers). If the modeled interface involves the GRM8 extracellular domain, glycans could interfere, but this is secondary to the expression mismatch.
cooccurrence_evidence: 0 PubMed co-mentions.
known_interaction_evidence: STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction (MRGPRX2 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. Nothing known for this pair.

follow_up: Deprioritize. If pursued: (1) inspect whether the interface is transmembrane-helix packing, a common AF3 membrane-protein artifact since no bilayer is modeled, or involves the GRM8 extracellular domain; (2) check for real spatial co-localization of GRM8+ cells with mast cells (e.g. meningeal or choroid plexus mast cells) before any wet-lab test; (3) fold MRGPRX2 against unrelated GPCRs as a specificity control.

rationale: The pair is novel (no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed hit) and the AF3 score is moderate (ipTM 0.65, interface pLDDT 68.7). But HEBP1 is a predicted intracellular haem-binding protein and GPR37 is a 7TM GPCR with a glycosylated ectodomain, and I could not determine which face of GPR37 the modelled interface sits on. fold_complex was not available in this session, so no topology check was run. Without it the compartment mismatch is a soft negative, and GPR37's own HPA localisation is rated Uncertain.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: GPR37 is a UniProt Glycoprotein with 3 glycosylation sites, 1 disulfide and Ubl conjugation; N-glycan sites on a GPCR are normally extracellular. If the modelled interface is on the extracellular face, glycans could occlude it and HEBP1 would also be on the wrong side of the membrane. HEBP1 has no annotated PTM features. cooccurrence_evidence: 0 PubMed co-mentions.

A purely cytoplasmic interface would be a plausible novel intracellular docking interaction. Separately, from background knowledge rather than the tools: an N-terminal HEBP1 peptide (F2L) is reported to be a secreted agonist of the GPCR FPR3, so it may be worth folding the HEBP1 N-terminal peptide alone against GPR37, with the known ligand prosaposin (PSAP) as a positive control. Wet-lab confirmation would be co-IP or BRET in oligodendrocyte-lineage cells. GPR37's 63 HPA-listed interactors suggest a hub, so specificity controls are needed.

rationale: The flagged problem is real. The AF3 interface for GNRH2-MRGPRX2 includes both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues of MRGPRX2, which cannot happen across an intact membrane. The fold therefore gives no support for a binding mode, and I give it no credit toward CONFIRMED_NOVEL or LIKELY_SUBCOMPLEX. It is a flaw in this one model, probably from folding the unprocessed GnRH-II precursor, not evidence about the biology, so on its own it does not justify IMPLAUSIBLE. HPA expression is plausible and nothing shows the two proteins cannot meet, but STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed all returned nothing for this pair (strength: none). Plausible expression alone is not interaction evidence. With a discredited structure, no literature or database support, and no evidence against, the pair is neither confirmed nor ruled out.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: No relevant glycosylation for either protein. Mature GnRH-II is a processed, amidated, pyroglutamyl decapeptide, which AF3 did not model. That is another reason to distrust the fold interface.
cooccurrence_evidence: 0 PubMed papers mention GNRH2 and MRGPRX2 together.
known_interaction_evidence: STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed co-occurrence returned nothing for this pair (strength: none).
follow_up: Re-fold with the mature GnRH-II decapeptide (pyroGlu-His-Trp-Ser-His-Gly-Trp-Tyr-Pro-Gly-NH2) against MRGPRX2. Accept only a pose confined to the extracellular or transmembrane pocket. Alternatively, test experimentally whether GnRH-II activates MRGPRX2, for example in a mast cell degranulation or calcium assay.

rationale: My original rationale said the fold showed no membrane-topology violation. That was wrong. The fold flagged a topology_violation: the whole GHRL–MRGPRX4 interface sits on the cytoplasmic face of MRGPRX4, and ghrelin is a secreted peptide that cannot reach the cytoplasm. The modeled contact is therefore not physiologically possible. The other evidence does not rescue it. HPA says the pair is "plausible" because a secreted hormone and a plasma-membrane GPCR could meet in principle, but that does not make this pose real. Known-interaction strength is none: STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed co-occurrence all returned nothing. The ipTM of 0.65 is modest and the partner pLDDT of 47.7 is low. The PTM concern (ghrelin octanoylation/amidation, MRGPRX4 glycosylation) was not at the interface, and neither protein is a lectin, so the PTM and glycan-mediated override does not apply. I now treat the prediction as an AF3 artifact, not a novel interaction. Ghrelin's real receptor is GHSR, and MRGPRX4 is a bile-acid/itch receptor. I am not fully certain because ghrelin could in theory contact MRGPRX4's extracellular face, but the modeled interface is not that.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: Ghrelin has octanoylation and amidation. MRGPRX4 has 2 glycosylation sites. None are at the modeled interface, and neither protein is a lectin, so a PTM artifact is not the main problem. The topology violation is.
cooccurrence_evidence: PubMed co-occurrence returned 0 papers for GHRL and MRGPRX4.
known_interaction_evidence: STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no hit (MRGPRX4 is not in its table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. No known-interaction support.
follow_up: If this pair is still of interest, re-fold with the mature octanoylated ghrelin peptide and check that the contact is on the extracellular or transmembrane-pocket face of MRGPRX4. A cytoplasmic-face pose should be rejected.

rationale: The pair is novel (no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed hit) and both are plasma-membrane proteins with some bone-marrow overlap, so a cis interaction is topologically possible. I could not verify whether any glycosite sits on the interface because no fold tool was available in this session, so this is an unresolved caveat rather than a demonstrated artifact; the moderate ipTM (0.64) and borderline p_twoway (0.053) do not offset it.

PVR and NECTIN2 are listed under other_subunits only as known CD226 ligands for that competition check, not as missing complex members.

rationale: The pair is novel (no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed hit) and biologically plausible as a trans contact between two plasma-membrane proteins. GPR141: Glycoprotein keyword with 2 glycosylation sites, which I assume (not checked per-residue) lie on the extracellular N-terminus or loops. The PubMed PTM searches were mostly non-specific (17 hits for SIGLEC1, including sialylated CD43; 1 unrelated hit for GPR141). Whether any glycosylation site sits on the modeled interface was not checked.

known_interaction_evidence: STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction (GPR141 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is unreported.
follow_up: No fold was run. Map the modeled interface residues onto UniProt topology and glycosylation sites to confirm the contact is extracellular-to-extracellular and whether the SIGLEC1 V-set sialic-acid site or GPR141's N-glycan sites are involved. Re-fold with glycans attached at the GPR141 N-glycosylation sites. Test experimentally with SIGLEC1-Fc binding to GPR141-expressing cells with and without sialidase, and with the sialic-acid-binding-dead SIGLEC1 mutant (R116A in the V-set domain, residue number recalled from the literature, not retrieved here). TYROBP is listed under other subunits only because UniProt mentions it as a SIGLEC1 signalling partner; it is not established as an obligate subunit. With 2014 tokens and pTM 0.38, the long SIGLEC1 Ig-repeat chain is poorly placed overall; a fold restricted to the N-terminal domains would be cleaner.

rationale: The fold check found a topology violation. The modeled interface (BSA 5310 Å2, 1124 contacts, partner pLDDT 58) spans both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues of the membrane protein. My earlier INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE verdict did not account for this. Other evidence also points away from a real interaction. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed all show no prior link. The one remaining route is a genuine extracellular contact between the EFNA3 ectodomain and the GPR21 N-terminus or loops, and nothing supports that. The fold is low-confidence and the prediction is an artifact of unconstrained topology, so I downgrade to IMPLAUSIBLE. Confidence is medium because the absence of data is not proof that the proteins never interact.

rationale: The real AF3 fold shows the CHL1–GPR12 interface spanning both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues. rationale: CATSPER2 is a pore-forming subunit of the sperm-specific CatSper channel in the sperm flagellum (UniProt; HPA end piece/principal piece), while GPR25 is a lymphocyte chemokine receptor for CXCL17 with HPA enrichment only in stomach, so there is no shared cell type for two integral membrane proteins that would have to meet in the same membrane. No STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed link exists, and the ipTM of 0.63 between a 6-TM channel subunit and a 7-TM GPCR is most likely generic helix-helix packing, with CATSPER2's obligate CatSper partners absent from the model.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: UniProt lists no glycosylation or lipidation features for either protein (GPR25 has one disulfide bond only). The PubMed PTM search returned 2 hits for CATSPER2, neither about its modifications, and 0 for GPR25. There is no PTM basis for an artifact call; the concern is biological context and unmodeled membrane/complex.
cooccurrence_evidence: pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 hits for CATSPER2 and GPR25.
known_interaction_evidence: STRING: no association found. CellPhoneDB: no curated interaction, and GPR25 is not in its gene table. PubMed co-occurrence: 0 papers. The pair is unreported, but that novelty does not outweigh the biological mismatch.
follow_up: No fold was run for this candidate. If it is pursued anyway: (1) inspect the existing model to see whether the interface is purely TM-helix packing; (2) re-fold CATSPER2 with its CatSper partners (CATSPER1/3/4 pore subunits, plus CATSPERB/CATSPERD from CellPhoneDB) to see whether the GPR25 contact surface is already occupied in the native channel; (3) check sperm proteomics for any GPR25 expression. rationale: The contradiction is valid. PPIA was folded against 11 receptors and passed the confidence gate for 4 of them (36%), so the moderate AF3 result (ipTM 0.62) for GPR3 mostly reflects PPIA, not GPR3. PPIA is a small, abundant, sticky cyclophilin. The breadth here is not a shared-receptor pattern like a chemokine's, because PPIA has no known promiscuous GPCR-ligand role. Its one established extracellular partner is BSG/CD147, which is not a GPCR. That makes the breadth look like a non-specific fold artifact, and I withdraw CONFIRMED_NOVEL. The other evidence does not rescue specificity. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed co-occurrence are all empty (known_interaction_strength=none), so there is no prior support for this pair. HPA plausibility is only 'plausible', with no subcellular data, so co-localization is not substantiated. The GPR3 glycosylation and palmitoylation sites are unmodeled and unchecked against the interface. I do not call the pair IMPLAUSIBLE, since PPIA is secreted and GPR3 is a surface GPCR. The pair is currently uninformative.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: GPR3 has 1 glycosylation site and 1 palmitoylation site, and PPIA has 1 glycosylation site. AF3 does not model these, and their position relative to the interface was not checked. This matters only if the interface is extracellular.
cooccurrence_evidence: PubMed co-occurrence count is 0 for PPIA and GPR3.
known_interaction_evidence: STRING not found; CellPhoneDB no entry (GPR3 absent); PubMed co-occurrence 0 hits. No prior evidence of interaction, so this is not ALREADY_KNOWN, but absence also gives no positive support.

Compare GPR3's ipTM with PPIA to its ipTM with other partners. Check which side of the membrane the interface sits on, and whether the GPR3 glycosylation site is near it. Obtain HPA subcellular data for both proteins.

rationale: The fold check shows the predicted FN1–GPR82 interface covers both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues of GPR82. I am therefore downgrading from CONFIRMED_NOVEL to IMPLAUSIBLE. A real extracellular-only FN1–GPR82 contact is not excluded, but nothing here supports one.

rationale: The fold check shows a glycosylation/lipidation site lying directly on the modeled B2M–GPR82 interface. My earlier CONFIRMED_NOVEL verdict left this unchecked, and the flagged site undercuts it. AF3 models bare sequence, so a contact that runs through a glycosylated residue (GPR82 has 2 UniProt glycosylation sites, likely on the extracellular face) may not be a real binding mode. The glycan could block the contact or change it. The pair is still novel, with no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed trace (known_interaction_strength=none). But ipTM 0.51, interface pLDDT 64.9 and min PAE 9.3 Å are weak, so the interface is not strong enough to outweigh the PTM concern. I therefore downgrade to a PTM-caveated artifact. The confident-novel call is not justified.

rationale: No prior evidence links this pair (STRING not found, CellPhoneDB not found, 0 PubMed co-mentions), and expression/compartment do not rule it out. However, IGF2R's documented binding mechanism is lectin-type (mannose-6-phosphate recognition) and its ectodomain carries 18 annotated glycosylation sites, while GPR82 has 2 on its small extracellular surface; AF3's bare-sequence model represents none of this. The fold itself is also weak (ipTM 0.51 at the threshold, interface pLDDT 52.4, min separation 1.79 Å suggesting clashes), so the modeled interface is not trustworthy as drawn. I could not check whether any glycosylation site actually sits on the modeled interface, so the artifact call rests on general plausibility, not a per-residue finding.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: IGF2R (UniProt P11717): Glycoprotein, Lipoprotein/Palmitate; 18 glycosylation sites, 59 disulfide bonds; function is binding phosphomannosyl (M6P) residues on lysosomal enzymes, i.e. a glycan-mediated mechanism. GPR82 (Q96P67): Glycoprotein with 2 glycosylation sites. The PubMed PTM search gave 56 hits for IGF2R (the top titles are mostly not about PTMs) and 0 for GPR82. With about 2,832 Å² of buried surface on the heavily glycosylated IGF2R ectodomain, glycan interference at the modeled contact is plausible, but whether any site lies on the interface was not checked.
cooccurrence_evidence: pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 papers mentioning IGF2R and GPR82 together.
known_interaction_evidence: STRING: no association found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction found (GPR82 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is unreported; GPR82 is an orphan receptor per UniProt.
follow_up: Map the modeled interface residues against IGF2R's 18 and GPR82's 2 UniProt N-glycosylation sites, and check membrane topology of the interface (that it does not combine cytoplasmic and extracellular residues). Re-fold using only the relevant IGF2R domain repeats plus GPR82, with glycans attached, to see whether ipTM rises clearly above 0.5; the current 2,827-token fold with interface pLDDT 52 and 1.79 Å minimum separation is marginal. IGF2R has 116 known interactors (HPA), so a promiscuous or non-specific contact with a large ectodomain is also possible. If the interface survives, test by co-immunoprecipitation in macrophage/Kupffer-like cells.

rationale: I'm changing the verdict from INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE to IMPLAUSIBLE, because two points now count against the pair and nothing counts for it. (1) Neither protein is secreted, and HPA shows no shared protein-level tissue. The only overlap is RNA-level, in smooth muscle cells and pericytes. I had treated that overlap and the poor antibody coverage for GPCRs as reasons to stay neutral. Without protein evidence, though, there is no substantiated way for the two to meet. Being plasma-membrane proteins in general does not supply one. (2) A real AF3 fold was run, which my original triage did not account for. It placed the A–B interface across both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues. That is topologically impossible across an intact membrane, so the predicted contact is not a physical interaction. The interface also sits on a glycosylation or lipidation site, and AF3 does not model those modifications. The pair has no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed support, and no other evidence offsets these concerns. Confidence is medium and not high because the HPA gap partly reflects limited antibody coverage and RNA overlap does exist.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: CSPG4 has 16 glycosylation sites and MRGPRF has 1. The fold flagged a glycosylation or lipidation site directly on the modeled interface, so the bare-sequence contact is unreliable. Neither protein is a lectin.

follow_up: Check for protein-level co-localization of CSPG4 and MRGPRF in pericytes or vascular smooth muscle cells. Only if that is shown, re-fold with the ectodomains alone, so the interface cannot span the membrane, and model the glycans.

rationale: The flagged topology violation changes my verdict. The AF3 interface (4153 Å2, ipTM 0.5, partner pLDDT 51.7) spans both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues. The check also found a glycosylation or lipidation site directly on the modeled interface. There is no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed evidence of an interaction (known_interaction_strength = none). The fold gives no positive support either, so I now rate the pair implausible. It is not merely under-evidenced.

rationale: Both are integral membrane proteins (TFR2 single-pass type II, GPR22 a 7TM orphan GPCR), so a cis interaction needs the same cell, but HPA shows no overlap: TFR2 is liver-enriched (hepatocytes, erythrocyte progenitors) and GPR22 is in brain neurons and cardiomyocytes. The AF3 signal is borderline (ipTM 0.5, interface pLDDT 59.3, min separation 1.82 Å with 615 contacts and 3204 Å2 buried), which looks more like non-specific membrane-protein packing than a real interface. No STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed support exists; confidence is low because HPA has no localisation data for GPR22 and no fold was run to check interface topology.

The PubMed PTM searches returned nothing specific to glycosylation of either protein at an interface. Glycans on the extracellular regions are an extra caveat for any modeled ectodomain contact, but the verdict does not rest on this.

known_interaction_evidence: STRING: no association found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction, and GPR22 is not in its gene table. PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is unreported, but that novelty is not backed by biological plausibility.
follow_up: Deprioritise. The other_subunits listed are TFR2's physiological partners from general knowledge (it is a homodimer that binds transferrin and HFE), not from a tool result; CellPhoneDB returned no complex for either protein. If the pair is revisited, inspect the model for which regions form the interface (TM helix against TM helix, or an interface mixing cytoplasmic and extracellular residues, would indicate an artifact) and check whether the TFR2 glycosylation sites sit on it. Any real co-expression would most plausibly be in cardiomyocytes or neurons, where TFR2 is low, and should be confirmed before any wet-lab work.

rationale: My original rationale said the fold showed no topology violation. The check shows that was wrong. The fold put the CTSG–GPR34 interface on GPR34's cytoplasmic face. CTSG is a secreted granule protease with no membrane topology and no evidence of cytosolic localisation, so it cannot reach that face. The modeled contact is therefore not physically achievable, and the borderline confidence (ipTM about 0.5, interface pLDDT about 63) cannot rescue it. The remaining evidence is too thin to override this. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed show nothing for the pair (known_interaction_strength=none), and HPA co-expression is unknown, so nothing places the two proteins together. The only support is indirect: CTSG cleaves other GPCRs such as PAR1 and PAR4. A real interaction with GPR34's extracellular face stays conceivable, but this fold doesn't model it. I rate the modeled interaction implausible, with low confidence because that extracellular-face possibility was not tested.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: GPR34 has 5 UniProt N-glycosylation sites and CTSG has 2. None lie at the modeled interface. Neither protein is a lectin. The PTM concern is not the problem here; the topology violation is.
cooccurrence_evidence: 0 PubMed papers mention CTSG and GPR34 together.
known_interaction_evidence: STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed co-occurrence returned nothing for this pair (known_interaction_strength=none). CTSG acting on PAR1, PAR4 and FPR1 is only indirect precedent.
follow_up: Re-fold with constraints or a truncated GPR34 extracellular region (N-terminus and loops) against CTSG. Check whether a docked pose on the extracellular face is confident. Look at HPA immune-cell co-expression, for example neutrophils and mast cells.

rationale: The fold check shows a glycosylation or lipidation site sitting directly on the modeled PPIA–GPR63 interface. My original verdict left that unresolved, and the check now closes the gap. AF3 models bare sequence only, so any contact built around a modified residue may not match the real binding mode. This is most relevant for GPR63, an extracellular-facing GPCR with 3 UniProt glycosylation sites. It also fits my earlier concern that PPIA passed the confidence gate against 4 of 11 receptors, which points to partner-driven stickiness rather than specificity, and the ipTM of about 0.5 is only at threshold. The other evidence is unchanged: STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed show no prior record, so the pair is novel but unsupported, and HPA compartments are plausible. Plausible compartments do not offset a threshold-level fold whose interface depends on a modified residue. I am therefore moving from INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE to LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM, with medium confidence because I did not check whether the glycosylation site is on the GPR63 or PPIA side.

PPIA also binds heparan sulfate, which adds to the glycan concern.
